::: {#fig-newton-convergence}

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

### R

```{r}
#| label: newton-convergence-fig-r
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Line graph with the iteration number 0 to 3 on the horizontal axis and the
#|   error of the Newton iterate on a logarithmic vertical axis. Four blue
#|   points fall from 0.5 at iteration 0 to 0.05, then about 0.0006, then
#|   about 0.0000001, each drop larger than the last.
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-width: 5
nc_x_nc <- numeric(4)
nc_x_nc[1] <- 2.5
for (nc_t_nc in 1:3) {
  nc_prev_nc <- nc_x_nc[nc_t_nc]
  nc_x_nc[nc_t_nc + 1] <- 0.5 * (nc_prev_nc + 4 / nc_prev_nc)
}
nc_steps_nc <- tibble::tibble(t = 0:3, error = nc_x_nc - 2)
ggplot2::ggplot(nc_steps_nc, ggplot2::aes(t, error)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(colour = "#0072B2") +
  ggplot2::geom_point(colour = "#0072B2", size = 3) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_log10() +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "iteration t", y = "error of the iterate")
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: newton-convergence-fig-python
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Line graph with the iteration number 0 to 3 on the horizontal axis and the
#|   error of the Newton iterate on a logarithmic vertical axis. Four blue
#|   points fall from 0.5 at iteration 0 to 0.05, then about 0.0006, then
#|   about 0.0000001, each drop larger than the last.
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-width: 5
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

nc_x_ax = [2.5]
for _ in range(3):
    nc_x_ax.append(0.5 * (nc_x_ax[-1] + 4 / nc_x_ax[-1]))
nc_err_ax = [x - 2 for x in nc_x_ax]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3.5), layout="constrained")
ax.semilogy(range(4), nc_err_ax, "o-", color="#0072B2")
ax.set_xlabel("iteration t")
ax.set_ylabel("error of the iterate")
ax.set_xticks(range(4))
plt.show();
```

:::

The error $x^{(t)} - 2$ of @exm-newton-convergence on a logarithmic scale.
Each drop is steeper than the one before,
because the error is roughly squared at every step,
which is [quadratic convergence](#def-quadratic-convergence).

:::
